recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-17301; any future work on retired legacy clinical-document extensions belongs to the extension-pack/separate-extension issue path.
issue_request: FHIR-17301 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for R5 by Structured Documents. It asked to remove Composition.confidentiality because it duplicated security labels and to use/document a document Bundle's meta.security for clinical-document confidentiality or high-water-mark information.
initial_application: The original wrong-ballot FHIR-I tracker FHIR-14298 was cloned into FHIR-17301. PR #2027, merged as 4b84bbff405f4ce3233e2dd37d36a306205d85a5, and component commits f3e7ac34683c8671c4394b99790aa156564d279e and 44b8fc0d36fc16ff10da2eeb67ea80be49d05395 removed the Composition.confidentiality definition/search parameter and moved example labels to Bundle.meta.security. Commit ad98b08fee0ad580d40e0647f1f87858b231629b later added the Bundle.meta.security to ClinicalDocument.confidentialityCode mapping to the CDA comparison narrative.
additional_context: Composition is active in source/fhir.ini, but the legacy source/profiles/cda.profile.xml profile that still mentions Composition.confidentiality is commented out and not current-build input. Later Structured Documents work removed the active ClinicalDocument Composition profile under FHIR-34407, already represented on the combined branch, and FHIR-37719 minutes confirm related otherConfidentiality extension material belongs in Composition.meta.security or Bundle.meta.security. The current Extension Pack copy of otherConfidentiality is retired with a 'Use Bundle.meta.security instead' reason.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because active Composition source has no Composition.confidentiality element/search parameter/example use, document Bundle examples carry meta.security, the $document operation note describes the Bundle.meta.security high-water mark, and the active Composition CDA note maps Bundle.meta.security to ClinicalDocument.confidentialityCode.
